core_subsystem_gaps.area: Core state, context, event, service and runtime semantics
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native runtime implements state/event/service/storage contracts but is not the full HA Core runtime, event helper surface, job handling, entity lifecycle, or context propagation across every setup path.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Compare the full core/event/service tests and source semantics; extend Runtime without losing ordering, timestamps, error atomicity, contexts, subscriptions, and cancellation.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Startup, configuration, loader and config-entry lifecycle
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native config entries execute real registered setup/unload/retry/migration/config/options callbacks with persistent state and HTTP adapters. Typed subentry records now have stable parent-scoped identities, private data, source-compatible migration, registered native flows and post-commit lifecycle observers and a minimal durable removal-cleanup journal with exact-ID acknowledgement/startup replay; focused HTTP/WebSocket fixtures cover the public subset and persisted children. The 31 native hass-config cases also cover private, deduplicated, persisted DiscoveryKey values and deletion notifications for keys present at commit; SSDP observers run after the cleanup attempt, but the minimal subentry journal excludes SSDP keys and does not provide SSDP cleanup replay. Manifest-aware loading, complete dependency ordering, remaining discovery/platform flows, exhaustive pinned subentry acceptance and rollback/reload contracts remain open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Finish exhaustive pinned subentry migration, flow, lifecycle, privacy, role and error acceptance; then port manifest-aware setup, config-entry/data-flow state machines, deterministic dependency order, rollback, reload/unload, and failure/retry behavior before adding integration waves. Preserve SSDP's cleanup-after-attempt ordering and do not treat the separate minimal subentry journal as SSDP key replay.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Entity model, platforms and add/remove lifecycle
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Shared native provider identity, metadata refresh, weak leases, registry rename/disable/remove, restore and unload are exercised by actual template, clock, and Sun providers. Bounded Sun host review corrections have native and process checks; exhaustive Sun fixtures remain open. Sun Drop cleanup is best-effort unless joined shutdown is used. EntitySpec recording policy also omits Tag tag_id from state history while preserving full live state and state_changed payloads. Generic platform setup, polling/coordinator ownership, complete attribute/capability/domain semantics, translation and exhaustive failure/parity coverage remain open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Extend pinned Sun fixtures, provider replacement and failed-cleanup recovery checks; prove custom Store implementations honor the history projection; then extend the shared lifecycle to generic platform setup, coordinator refresh, source-complete attributes/capabilities and remaining providers against pinned entity tests.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Entity, device, area, floor and label registries
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native registry CRUD, provider metadata, service devices and validated references/events have fixtures. Composite migration splits active and deleted owner identities, retains complete legacy subentry associations, replaces copied identifiers once and resolves parent aliases through actual config-entry domains. Tag restart and injected rollback cases preserve live and removed identities. Remaining child-device behavior, categories, other registries and exhaustive payload acceptance remain open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Extend the accepted migration and identity guards against every pinned registry payload and child-device case; verify restart, collisions, invalid references, atomic persistence, websocket envelopes and event ordering.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Users, auth providers, refresh sessions, permissions and MFA
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native local password users, JWT/rotating refresh sessions, MFA enrollment/challenges/replay budgets, signed paths and live transport role checks have fixtures. External providers, custom per-entity permissions and all remaining auth/error contracts remain open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Keep secret-free public objects, prove hash/token/session persistence and rotation/revocation, reject disabled users, and port each pinned provider and role/permission boundary before claiming authentication parity.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: HTTP server, REST API, proxy trust and request safety
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native REST and WebSocket transports cover state/services/events/history/templates/auth and config flows with origin/proxy/local-only policy. Network adapter inventory/configuration and saved Core URL reads now use strict role-checked commands on the existing WebSocket dispatcher; they add no network HTTP route, service, or event. Repairs fix-flow and config-subentry flow routes have focused HTTP fixtures alongside WebSocket adapters for their supported commands. Remaining endpoints, IP bans, CORS, middleware/header, exact error and fine-grained permission parity stay open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Port each endpoint and middleware from pinned source; exercise trusted/untrusted proxy, invalid auth, rate/ban, body limits, status/error shapes, CORS and headers with local HTTP fixtures. Complete the remaining pinned network command, configuration and lifecycle acceptance with local WebSocket fixtures.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: WebSocket auth, command channels, subscriptions and payload contracts
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: System Log list/raw commands, Repairs issue/list/data/ignore commands, config-subentry list/update/delete commands, and the System Health system_health/info stream have native adapters and focused transport fixtures. Repairs changes use the ordinary public event path and native event history; subentry responses omit private data. System Health uses strict command fields, authenticated access for admin/ordinary/read-only identities, and joined callback cleanup on unsubscribe, disconnect, and shutdown. The admin-only SSDP feed adds a bounded callback queue with cached replay, live updates, overflow termination, unsubscribe and server-shutdown coverage. Only command subsets are available; remaining command families, per-feature authorization, flow lifecycle, message validation, subscription fan-out, exact event/result envelopes and exhaustive pinned acceptance remain open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Finish remaining pinned System Health provider/stream fixtures and Repairs/subentry command authorization, field, error and flow-lifecycle cases; then enumerate every remaining pinned command/channel, implement authorization and envelopes, and test malformed/duplicate IDs, auth expiry, subscriptions, shutdown and cleanup.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Recorder event/state pipeline, history, purge and statistics
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native SQLite state/event/private-metadata recording, multi-entity boundary history, purge/retention and actual repack have fixtures. Entity-specific StateRecordingPolicy omits Tag tag_id only from state-history snapshots; live/current state and generic event payloads retain it, including across SQLite reopen. Native generic event storage still records state_changed, unlike Home Assistant Recorder's state-row route, and the default Store::put_state_with_history ignores the projected snapshot unless a custom store overrides it. Complete ingestion/filter pipelines, long-term statistics, repairs, upstream migrations and other database backends remain open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Verify each custom Store override applies the state-history projection while preserving full events, then use pinned recorder migrations and tests to add event/state ingestion, filters, retention/purge, long-term statistics, migration/version refusal and query API semantics.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Automation, script, scene and template engines
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native scripts/scenes and shared action execution, state/event/numeric/template/time/MQTT/notification/lifecycle triggers, modes and reactive template entities have fixtures. Native Sun conditions, calculated-event scheduling, and rounded-state elevation changed/crossed cancellation have focused tests; source selector/unit, offset and trigger metadata corrections have passing checks. Exhaustive Sun fixtures and typed timedelta template methods remain open. Native tag_scanned callback triggers carry event context and metadata, with focused legacy composite-ID expansion coverage. Remaining trigger/condition/action/template surfaces, blueprints, traces and exhaustive acceptance remain open.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Extend pinned Sun and drive each engine from pinned tests: trigger/condition/action shapes and modes, script cancellation/queueing, scene snapshot/apply, template helper/filter semantics, resource limits and error behavior.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Native helper integrations, timer, button, datetime and schedules
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Five helper/service domains and several timer/button/datetime/schedule primitives exist, but standard integration configuration, entity lifecycle, restart/restore and exact events/services are not all accepted.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Port strict config validation, restore and services for each helper; use deterministic time and restart tests for timer, button timestamps, datetime/timezones and schedule edges; no physical state injection.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Frontend assets, translations, panels and frontend WebSocket workflows
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: The native server has no official frontend/assets or full frontend-facing API and dashboard/panel protocol. The SSDP adapter advertises no icon URLs until native icon assets are served.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Inventory and port the Core frontend API/asset-serving contract separately, including native SSDP icon assets and consumers; do not count API endpoint coverage as frontend parity.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Discovery, protocol managers, device events and transport lifecycles
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: A native adapter-address SDK now enumerates IPv4/IPv6 interfaces, persists selected adapter names and resolves a literal IPv4 route; SSDP consumes the selected addresses and applies its own protocol filter. A fixture-backed native SSDP protocol, manager, host and API stream also exists. The current port still has no accepted shared Bluetooth, Zigbee, Z-Wave, Matter/Thread, serial, USB, infrared or general discovery transport layer beyond SSDP and local adapter selection; the SSDP catalog's 44 domains and 94 matchers are metadata and do not establish driver ports.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Complete SSDP header-parser edge parity, uncommon text codecs, native icon serving, live adapter-change handling and pinned SSDP source acceptance; do not imply live socket rebinding or Supervisor reload debounce. Separately build fixture-backed shared transports and discovery lifecycle, then use the JSON protocol-family membership lists to port all dependent adapters.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Conversation, Assist pipeline, audio, camera and media-source subsystems
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: No native voice/conversation/audio/media/camera streaming pipeline is established by the current runtime or API implementation.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Port common streaming/provider contracts and bounds; prove with local protocol fixtures, deterministic audio/image data, reconnect, backpressure and cleanup.

core_subsystem_gaps.area: Backup, repairs, diagnostics, onboarding and system-level services
core_subsystem_gaps.gap: Native onboarding/password/MFA/login workflows and local persistence have fixtures. System Log list/write/raw-stream support is partial; its LLM consumers, coercion parity, observable overflow, reader-backed backlog and complete pinned acceptance remain open. Repairs now has a partial native registry/fix-flow manager, HTTP/WebSocket subset, post-commit host lifecycle and actual-process persistence/event/confirmation/restart evidence. System Health now has a native provider SDK, authenticated system_health/info stream, core native-version/current-timezone callback, privacy-safe config warning, and focused protocol/process evidence; only the core provider is included, and full pinned provider coverage, Python/platform discovery, frontend/LLM metadata and real external health probes remain open. Arbitrary provider callback values remain generic and source-compatible for authenticated readers without blanket redaction. Cross-document cleanup uses a minimal durable removal journal with startup replay and exact-ID acknowledgement; replay does not backfill public change events and cross-document writes remain non-atomic; fine-grained POLICY_EDIT, exhaustive pinned acceptance, frontend/translations, Python loader, and real provider activity remain open. Backup/restore, diagnostics and remaining system/frontend operating workflows are unported.
core_subsystem_gaps.next_acceptance: Complete the pinned Repairs storage, lifecycle, authorization, HTTP/WebSocket and failure acceptance; expand failure-recovery acceptance beyond the native registry/issue removal-cleanup journal; finish System Log LLM/coercion/dedup/overflow/backlog parity; and expand System Health beyond the native core callback with full pinned provider, stream, Python/platform, frontend and LLM acceptance. Then port backup/restore, diagnostics and remaining system-service families with failure-safe persistence, authorization, restore/rollback and pinned API/test shape.

Partial native DHCP support exists in the uncommitted 35-crate workspace. The typed DHCP SDK includes the generated 386-row, 119-domain matcher catalog and 43 registered-device rules, preserving device-key presence even when its value is false. The wire decoder handles Ethernet IPv4/IPv6 UDP BOOTP requests, source MAC/IP and requested addresses, option semantics, and Python IDNA-2003 hostname decoding. The discovery crate provides bounded nonrecursive local DNS, route and neighbor data, named-only neighbor probes, ascending-host scans, and a 24-hour resolver-failure cache. Host setup requires explicit YAML-section presence, starts providers after startup, keeps empty adapter selection idle, restricts capture to selected adapters, and joins providers before dropping the SDK cache; typed private device-tracker publication and a version-1 WebSocket cache/update stream are also wired. Focused evidence lists 60 native tests and their exact symbols. Capture disables promiscuous mode but filters UDP in userspace, so it reads broader frames than a kernel BPF filter; raw packets are not logged. Implicit adapter selection is narrower than upstream default-interface behavior. The system scanner reads route/ARP data on Linux and reports unsupported on macOS; injected tests are portable. Other link-layer decoders, custom matcher loading, platform hot-rebinding, frontend behavior, and full pinned upstream acceptance remain open. The focused tests use synthetic or loopback fixtures only: no LAN traffic, live capture, external DNS, or production provider activity. The current 35-crate workspace passes 874 tests across 100 targets with zero failures or ignored tests; strict locked offline workspace all-target Clippy and formatting pass. A fresh binary-focused run passes 126 tests. The 35-crate local release build and optimized CLI checks pass for the example and empty, ignored-DHCP, false-DHCP, and invalid-root-key configurations without database creation. The macOS candidate binary SHA-256 is 3d7db1362393f27d411694fdb6c7b7c6a4a7bfa60375f2aed0591caa93e6b8172. No 35-crate commit or CI receipt is claimed.

A native adapter SDK and host integration enumerate IPv4/IPv6 addresses, retain configured names, persist selections atomically, reload selected snapshots, and resolve a literal IPv4 source address. Unknown or renamed configured names remain stored; reload applies only surviving exact names even if interface order changes. IPv6 scope IDs are preserved (including zero), while flowinfo is cleared to zero. The WebSocket surface is limited to `network` (admin inventory), `network/configure` (admin preferences; an omitted config defaults to `{}`), and `network/url` (any authenticated user receives saved Core URLs and cloud `null`); no network event, service, or HTTP route is added. SDK tests use injected providers; the actual-process fixture uses SystemAdapterEnumerator plus UDP connect/read-local-address without sending, and temporary SQLite writes preferences only. This does not alter OS interfaces or perform LAN discovery. SSDP consumes the selected network addresses before its own protocol filter, with selection captured at startup; live socket rebinding and Supervisor reload debounce are not claimed. Platform limits remain: if-addrs nice_name mappings are not exact on every platform, IPv6 flowinfo defaults to zero with inferred scope, and route resolution is literal-IPv4-only. Full pinned Python/provider, UI and network lifecycle acceptance remain open.

Partial native parity is evidenced by the Rust SSDP SDK, shared manager/cache/scanner/server, native host integration, typed config-entry discovery identity, and an admin-only bounded WebSocket callback stream with cancellable cleanup. The host now consumes addresses selected by the native Network SDK and then applies the SSDP protocol filter; that selection is captured at startup, and live socket rebinding or Supervisor reload debounce is not claimed. The wildcard listener receives multicast M-SEARCH on loopback, and /device.xml HEAD requests preserve the GET content length with an empty body. Description lookup fetches the first observed location and evaluates the latest headers after HTTP; live notifications retain the first location while getters and replay follow the current header location. Tracking uses UTC instants while public timestamp metadata follows the dependency's naive local microsecond shape. Callbacks remain private and do not become Runtime history. Remaining acceptance includes exact pinned fixture parity, header-parser edge behavior, uncommon Python text codecs, native frontend icon assets/consumers, live adapter-change lifecycle and any uncovered pinned source behavior. The bundled 44-domain/94-matcher metadata catalog does not establish those integrations as ported. SERVER/model/version values describe the Rust implementation, and no icon URLs are advertised until native assets are served. Evidence is limited to synthetic datagrams and loopback HTTP/UDP/WebSocket fixtures; no physical device, production-interface activity, or live provider traffic is claimed.
